notes: Espressif is the reference part; AliExpress modules generally work fine too. If yours shows the cold-boot issue, one 10k GPIO0 pullup on the module fixes it (Issue #16). Do NOT solder the DevKit itself; it plugs into the female sockets.
Not a separate PCB refdes. Solder two socket rows into the U1 header-hole rows; the DevKit plugs in on top.

CRITICAL: insert from the BACK side — encoder bodies on back, leads soldered on front. 20mm shaft: print knobs from hardware/case/knobs/knobs_20mm.stl. Any 5-pin EC11 with a push switch works — the cheapest packs just fail more often. Substitute only if mechanically equivalent for PCB/enclosure fit.

Widely available at retail too — search 'TYPE-C 14P CC-2.6'. ⚠️ The THT signal-pin soldering is genuinely difficult; a bridge here has shorted and burned a board (Issue #114). Beginners: skip USB1 + R1/R2 entirely and populate J4 instead.
USB-C CC pull-downs (sink). Only needed if USB1 is populated. Any 5.1kΩ 1/4W axial resistor works.
HUB75 ribbon to the LED matrix. Mechanical orientation must match PCB silkscreen/footprint.
+5V output to the LED matrix. Required on every build. Equivalent part acceptable only if pitch and footprint match.
Beginner power-input bypass on the BACK of the board: strip a standard USB cable and screw the wires in, instead of soldering USB1. Populate USB1 or J4 (or both).
Main bulk decoupling. Observe polarity. Equivalent part acceptable only if size/lead spacing fits the PCB.
